findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> (or a domain error enum) and propagate fs::read_to_string with ? or match

findings.failure_mode: malformed audit line causes panic instead of returning a typed parse error for downstream handling
findings.fix: use parts[1].parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...) and return Result<Vec<Record>, E> with a domain parse error type

findings.problem: as u16 cast from u32 is lossy and silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value outside u16 range wraps or truncates silently, producing a corrupted Record with no error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and propagate the error via TryFrom, or parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>()

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing with no bounds verification
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields panics on index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed validation error
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1) with map_err, or split_once(',') to parse exactly one separator

findings.problem: println!("loaded ...") is a side-effecting I/O call mixed into a parsing function
findings.failure_mode: pure data transformation is polluted with logging side effects, making the function non-deterministic and untestable without capturing stdout
findings.fix: remove println! from the core parsing logic; if logging is needed, push it to the shell layer that calls this function

findings.problem: load_audits mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing, validation, and logging in a single function
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be unit-tested for parsing correctness without mocking the filesystem, and cannot be reused for in-memory audit data
findings.fix: split into pure parse_audit_line(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and shell-level load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that handles I/O and delegates to the pure parser

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 with no domain validation at construction
findings.failure_mode: any code can create a Record with an empty name or out-of-range value, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: add a fn new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError> that validates constraints, or use newtype wrappers like newtype!(RecordName, String)

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> with map+collect allocates intermediate vectors per line
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per line degrade throughput for high-volume audit files
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get exactly two parts, then &part.trim().to_string() or borrow with &str until final collection

findings.problem: Collecting all parts with .collect() into Vec<String> when only the first two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: each line allocates a Vec and multiple Strings even for simple 2-field records, wasting memory and GC pressure
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') to get exactly two parts, then trim and use each individually without collecting

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for stated or implied throughput claims of load_audits
no profiler data (cargo-flamegraph, perf, or similar) to validate allocation patterns
no allocation audit (e.g., cargo-bench with --benchmarks or jemalloc profiling) for the hot path
no second-ring testing (Kani, Miri, or property tests) to verify no panics on malformed input
no command-line interface evidence or integration test demonstrating correct error handling end-to-end
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. This crate has fundamental architectural issues: I/O and parsing are fused in one function, forbidden constructs (unwrap, unchecked indexing, lossy cast) dominate every line, and the domain model has no validation. Even a minimal refactoring to pure parser + shell split + Result return types would resolve the majority of blockers.
